Finding.Text: New, introduced by the last commit. check no longer examines a brief unless its grace5:contract-sha256 meta already equals the current contract hash; before, the brief of the current revision was always examined. brief.md says the mechanical check runs on every brief and that its first rule is that this meta equals the contract's hash. Probe: a brief of the current revision that omits a protected path makes check exit 1 with the FS-14 defect; delete its hash meta line, or change the hash, and check exits 0 with no defect line, status shows approved for execution, and run --start executes. The commonest way to reach this needs no tampering: the author edits the contract to resolve the brief writer's findings and the brief is not brought up to the new text. check then reports nothing, where the prepare skill has the owner read nothing only while check reports a defect, so the owner can be handed a brief written for other contract text with a clean check. close still refuses at step 2 (brief does not match the approval), so nothing closes falsely; what is lost is the one mechanical guard before the owner gate, and it is found only after the work is done. The rule that reports a wrong or missing hash in briefDefects can no longer be reached from check. The change was made so that an altered contract does not stop its bound checks now that run refuses on every defect (restoring the old rule turns FL-08 red); commands.md rule 6 can be read to allow it, and brief.md cannot. No test covers a current-revision brief with a wrong or missing hash.

New, from the same commit. run now refuses on any blocking defect before it looks at the authorization. Probe: with revision 2 awaiting approval and a draft brief-2 that has a fidelity defect, run refuses outright, although authorization.md says a check the last approved revision bound still runs while a revision awaits approval; before brief-2 was written the same run executed CK1. commands.md, as amended, says every such defect makes run refuse, so the two documents now pull apart. The commit message does not mention this change or the one in F17, and the run help text does not mention that defects hold a run.
